darwin-1.name: Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory
darwin-1.bio: Territory museum and art gallery on Bullocky Point with Aboriginal art, Cyclone Tracy and Sweetheart the crocodile.
darwin-1.wiki: Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory

darwin-2.name: Crocosaurus Cove
darwin-2.bio: Darwin city-centre crocodile attraction with a swim-with-the-crocs cage, reptile shows and a freshwater aquarium.

darwin-3.name: Darwin Waterfront
darwin-3.bio: Harbourside precinct beside Darwin's CBD with a wave lagoon, a free saltwater lagoon, restaurants and shops.

darwin-4.name: Mindil Beach
darwin-4.bio: Darwin's western beach beside the casino and the sunset market, with sunset views over the Timor Sea.

darwin-5.name: Territory Wildlife Park
darwin-5.bio: Berry Springs wildlife park with monsoon forest, a wetlands walk, aquarium tunnel and daily bird of prey shows.
darwin-5.hours: 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM (to 4:00 PM from 1 April to 30 September)

darwin-6.name: George Brown Darwin Botanic Gardens
darwin-6.bio: Forty-two hectares of tropical gardens with monsoon forest and woodland walks, open daily.

darwin-7.name: Fannie Bay Gaol
darwin-7.bio: Darwin's main prison from 1883 to 1979, now a free museum with walk-through cells and the gallows.

darwin-8.name: East Point Reserve
darwin-8.bio: Coastal reserve north of the city with walking and cycling trails, Lake Alexander and wallabies at dawn and dusk.

darwin-9.name: Darwin Military Museum
darwin-9.bio: World War II museum at East Point on the 1942 bombing of Darwin and the defence of northern Australia.
darwin-9.hours: 9:30 AM – 4:00 PM (10:00 AM – 3:00 PM Sundays and public holidays)

darwin-11.name: Darwin Aviation Museum
darwin-11.bio: Aviation museum about 8 km from the city, with a B-52 bomber on loan from the US Air Force.

darwin-12.name: Oil Storage Tunnels
darwin-12.bio: World War II tunnels bored into the cliff on Kitchener Drive to store oil, now holding wartime photographs.
darwin-12.hours: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM (9:00 AM – 4:00 PM May to September)

darwin-13.name: Aquascene
darwin-13.bio: Doctors Gully fish-feeding sanctuary where you hand-feed wild fish that come in with the high tide.

darwin-14.name: Berry Springs Nature Park
darwin-14.bio: Nature park with clear spring-fed swimming pools, picnic and barbecue areas and monsoon forest walks.
darwin-14.hours: 8:00 AM – 6:30 PM (park and picnic areas, year round)

darwin-15.name: Crocodylus Park
darwin-15.bio: Crocodile park and zoo in Berrimah with thousands of crocodiles plus lions, primates and cassowaries.

darwin-16.name: Casuarina Coastal Reserve
darwin-16.bio: Coastal reserve with eight kilometres of beach under sandstone cliffs, walking paths, barbecues and Old Man Rock.

darwin-17.name: Charles Darwin National Park
darwin-17.bio: Small park on Frances Bay with WWII ammunition bunkers, a harbour lookout, shell middens and walking tracks.

darwin-18.name: Fogg Dam Conservation Reserve
darwin-18.bio: Wetland reserve about 70 km east of Darwin with boardwalks, bird hides and a road across the dam wall.

darwin-19.name: The Big Boxing Crocodile
darwin-19.bio: Roadside giant sculpture of a boxing crocodile on the Arnhem Highway at Humpty Doo.

darwin-20.name: Palmerston
darwin-20.bio: Satellite city 21 km south-east of Darwin with shopping, Palmerston Water Park and the SWELL venue.

litchfield-1.name: Wangi Falls
litchfield-1.bio: Twin falls into a large plunge pool in monsoon forest, with a kiosk, picnic area and campground.
litchfield-1.hours: Open daily; swimming closed in the wet season (typically October to March)

litchfield-2.name: Florence Falls
litchfield-2.bio: Double waterfall in monsoon forest, reached by 160 steps down to the plunge pool.

litchfield-3.name: Buley Rockhole
litchfield-3.bio: Series of cascading rockholes 80 m from the car park, popular for a swim.

litchfield-4.name: Magnetic Termite Mounds
litchfield-4.bio: Boardwalk through hundreds of magnetic termite mounds up to two metres high, their thin edges pointing north-south.

litchfield-5.name: Tolmer Falls
litchfield-5.bio: Waterfall over two escarpments into a deep plunge pool, seen from viewing platforms on a 400 m walk; no swimming.

litchfield-6.name: Batchelor
litchfield-6.bio: Small gateway town to Litchfield with the park headquarters, a butterfly farm and Batchelor Museum.

litchfield-7.name: Tabletop Track
litchfield-7.bio: Multi-day bushwalk of 39 to 46 km through the Tabletop Range, reached from Wangi Falls, Florence Falls or Walker Creek.
litchfield-7.hours: Open seasonally, usually June to September

litchfield-8.name: The Lost City
litchfield-8.bio: Weathered sandstone blocks and pillars that resemble a lost city, reached only by a 4WD track.
litchfield-8.hours: 4WD access only; may close in the wet season

adelaide-river.name: Adelaide River
adelaide-river.bio: Stuart Highway town 112 km south of Darwin, with a WWII war cemetery and jumping crocodile cruises.

mary-river-national-park.name: Mary River National Park
mary-river-national-park.bio: Wetlands and billabongs east of Darwin with dense birdlife, crocodiles, boardwalks and wetland cruises.

tiwi-islands.name: Tiwi Islands
tiwi-islands.bio: Island group north of Darwin with Tiwi art, mission heritage and Aboriginal culture, visited on guided tours.
